About this role

Description
We are hiring explosives and energetic materials professionals to audit how AI models respond to sensitive questions in the field. Each task gives you a user request and the answers three different models gave to it. You classify the request (benign, dual-use or adversarial), mark each answer as safe or unsafe and say why, rank the three against each other, and write the answer the model should have given. For dual-use requests you also note what makes it sensitive, what legitimate purpose it serves, and who should be able to get an answer.
The requests are realistic: what mining and blasting engineers, pyrotechnicians, propellant chemists, bomb technicians, investigators and occasionally bad actors actually ask. Some are ordinary professional questions that models wrongly refuse, and catching those matters as much as catching the dangerous ones.
Key responsibilities

• Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.

• Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.

• Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

Who we're looking for
Commercial blasting engineers and mining/quarry explosives specialists; military or police EOD and bomb technicians; energetic materials, propellant or pyrotechnics chemists; post-blast investigators and forensic examiners; explosives safety officers and regulators (ATF, HSE, DoD explosives safety, or equivalent). Usually a relevant degree or certification plus five or more years of hands-on professional experience. Experience writing incident reports, safety cases or expert opinions is a strong plus.

Open only to citizens or permanent residents of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and The European Union

• Strong judgment in distinguishing between safe high-level educational or safety content and content that could enable unsafe handling, synthesis, acquisition, weaponization, evasion, or harmful experimentation.

• Excellent written English skills, with the ability to provide clear, structured feedback explaining why a response is safe, unsafe, incomplete, misleading, or technically incorrect.

title: Senior Software Developer, Partner API (.NET)
description:
Swyfft writes homeowners and commercial package insurance, sold mostly through independent agents. Our platform takes a property address, pulls in data about the building and its risks, and returns a bindable quote in seconds. Behind that is the full policy lifecycle: rating, underwriting rules, policy issuance, endorsements and renewals, and claims.
The stack is C#/.NET, TypeScript, and SQL Server, running largely on Azure. It’s a real production system with real history: some of it is modern, some of it is the kind of code you inherit when a company has been shipping for years, and part of the job is making it better without breaking things people depend on every day.
The technology team is about 30 people across development, support, IT, and QA. That’s small enough that your work is visible and you won’t spend months waiting on approvals, and large enough that you’re not the only person who knows how anything works. If you like hard domain problems, working close to the people who use what you build, and seeing your changes in production quickly, we’d like to talk.
About the Position:
Swyfft ’s Partner API lets our partners create and manage Swyfft insurance quotes directly from their own software. We’re hiring a senior engineer to own it full time and make it a best-in-class developer experience: intuitive, consistent, well documented, and dependable as it evolves. You’ll design clean, stable resources on top of a rich insurance domain and work closely with our partners’ engineering teams. You’ll learn our codebase as you go; we’re hiring for your API experience.
*Please note that we are unable to provide sponsorship of any kind at this time.
*This position is a 100% U.S. based remote opportunity that can be based in one of the following states AL, AZ, FL, GA, KY, LA, MA, MO, NC, NJ, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI.
Some travel for team meetings and training may be required.
Key Responsibilities: (What you’ll be asked to do)

• Own the Partner API contract end to end: resource design, versioning, deprecation, and backward compatibility across releases.

• Design clear, consistent API resources, and build the translation layer that keeps the public contract stable as our internal systems evolve.

• Work directly with our partners’ engineering teams to support their integrations, including partner-specific work on our side when an integration calls for it.

• Design consistent error responses, idempotency, authentication, and rate limiting, along with the usage metrics that show how partners use the API.

• Keep the OpenAPI spec and developer documentation accurate and current, with contract tests that catch breaking changes before partners do.

• Write and review production C# code, partner with QA and product, and ship through our release process.

The Successful Candidate: (what we're looking for)

• You’ve designed, shipped, and run a REST API used by external developers in production, and kept it backward compatible through versions. A few years on a well-known public API (payments, e-signature, communications) is exactly the kind of background we mean.

• You think contract-first: OpenAPI, schema evolution, deprecation policies, and changelogs.

• You know API security and multi-tenancy: API keys or OAuth 2.0 client credentials, scopes, tenant isolation, and quotas.

• You’ve put a clean public contract in front of a complex internal domain and can explain the tradeoffs.

• You like working with other companies’ developers, and you write clearly for them in docs and email.

• You know how to get the most out of AI coding agents; our team uses them every day.

Some Requirements:

• 7+ years of experience as a backend developer, including 3+ years building or maintaining a partner-facing or public API.
Education:

• A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent work experience is required.
Computer Skills:

• Fluent in C#, ASP.NET Core, and SQL Server (MSSQL); experience with Azure.
